title: Lunch-and-Learn: Exploring the Potential of Gemini Notebook for Teaching and Learning
description: Facilitators: Michele Vick, Center for Teaching Excellence Carlos Perez, Center for Teaching Excellence Description:  Discover how Gemini Notebook (formerly known as NotebookLM) can help you get more from the course materials you already have. In this interactive session, you will explore how Gemini Notebook can locate and summarize content, compare sources, generate teaching ideas, create lesson outlines, and answer questions grounded in your own documents. We will discuss best practices for using AI-generated content thoughtfully, including accessibility considerations. The workshop also includes examples of how students are using Gemini Notebook to support their learning and what that may mean for your teaching. This Lunch-and-Learn session includes a complimentary lunch provided by the Center for Teaching Excellence. Learning Outcomes: Participants will be able to… 1) Use Gemini Notebook to locate, summarize, and compare information from course materials. 2) Generate teaching resources, such as lesson outlines and instructional ideas, using Gemini Notebook. 3) Describe considerations for using Gemini Notebook responsibly in teaching and learning, including accessibility.

title: Lunch-and-Learn: Google Gems: Designing a Customized AI Assistant
description: Facilitators: Carlos Perez, Center for Teaching Excellence Dr. Jamie Thompson, Center for Teaching Excellence Description:  What if you had an assistant that knew your course, understood your grading policies, answered students' general questions, or helped them engage with course materials? Welcome to Gemini Gems, Google's AI that you can design to act as specialized assistant for your courses and workflows. In this hands-on workshop, you will build your own Gem from the ground up. You will learn how to design a custom assistant, upload course-specific resources such as your syllabus and instructional materials and refine your Gem's instructions and persona to align with your teaching goals. By the end of the session, you will leave with a fully functional, personalized AI assistant. Please bring a laptop and a few digital documents you use frequently (a syllabus, course lectures, or a grading rubric). This Lunch-and-Learn session includes a complimentary lunch provided by the Center for Teaching Excellence. Learning Outcomes: Participants will be able to… 1) Identify instructional possibilities of custom AI assistants. 2) Design a customized Gemini Gem. 3) Evaluate the Gem's responses and refine its performance.

description:
3MT Faculty & Staff Information Session: Preparing to Judge or Host a Practice 3MT Competition


  Interested in volunteering to judge at the Three Minute Thesis (3MT®) Preliminary Competition and want to learn more? Interested in hosting a practice competition for your students? Please join the Graduate & Professional School for a one-hour information session for faculty and staff interested in supporting their graduate and professional students development of their research communication skills through the Three Minute Thesis (3MT®) Competition hosted by the Graduate & Professional School.
  
  During this information session faculty and staff will learn:


  the goals of the 3MT Competition (created by the University of Queensland),
  
  key elements of the 3MT format,
  
  strategies for preparing graduate students to deliver effective presentations,
  
  best practices for judging a 3MT presentation to ensure fair, consistent, and constructive evaluation
  
  guidelines on how to host a mock competition (including receiving resources - judges instructions, rubric, etc.).

title: Academic English Communication Skills: Office Hours (Part 1)
description: This workshop prepares instructors whose primary language is not English for conducting effective office hours. Participants will explore undergraduate expectations and examine the core components of productive office hours. Through video analysis and small group discussion, attendees will learn best practices and common pitfalls in student consultations. The workshop emphasizes professional communication strategies, especially when addressing frustrated students. Additionally, the workshop will cover appropriate resources for student referrals, equipping TAs for successful and supportive office hour sessions. This is the first of two workshops in this series. title: Workshop: Dude, what’s your problem? Understanding problem framing to achieve good solutions.
description: All of us want to solve problems, and many of us pursue professional and civic pathways focused on problem-solving, whether that’s politics, engineering, business, or many, many other pursuits. However, we’re often not aware of the crucial step of problem-framing and how it determines the types of potential solutions that might be generated and their eventual success (or failure). In this workshop, participants will identify problems that plague their lives, look at past cases of effective and ineffective problem-framing and problem-solving, and consider how the problems they’ve identified can be framed to achieve different outcomes. The importance of this process will be underscored with applications in government, technology, business, and other fields.

title: Stop Refereeing Group Projects: A Plug-and-Play Toolkit for Student Self-Managing Teams
description: Facilitators: Nate Poling, Center for Teaching Excellence Description:This workshop explores how to design and facilitate small group projects that empower students to manage their own team dynamics, workflows, and internal conflicts. title: Workshop: Dude, what’s your problem? Understanding problem framing to achieve good solutions.
description: All of us want to solve problems, and many of us pursue professional and civic pathways focused on problem-solving, whether that’s politics, engineering, business, or many, many other pursuits. However, we’re often not aware of the crucial step of problem-framing and how it determines the types of potential solutions that might be generated and their eventual success (or failure). In this workshop, participants will identify problems that plague their lives, look at past cases of effective and ineffective problem-framing and problem-solving, and consider how the problems they’ve identified can be framed to achieve different outcomes. The importance of this process will be underscored with applications in government, technology, business, and other fields.

title: Workshop: Think Before You Click: A Look at Image Verification
description: They say a picture can speak a thousand words, if only those words were all true. In this age of misinformation, AI slop and doom scrolling it’s become easier than ever to consume images online that are misleading, mislabeled or completely false. This workshop will review basic image verification techniques by placing the audience in real breaking news scenarios. Participants will experience in real time how easy it is to share a bogus image and learn how to confirm its authenticity before hitting click.

title: Providing Students Multiple Pathways to Demonstrate Mastery
description: Facilitators: Justin Romack, Disability Resources Carlos Perez, Center for Teaching Excellence Description:The design of an assessment can affect how students demonstrate what they know and whether they have equal access to the assessment. By applying the principles of Universal Design for Learning (UDL), instructors can create flexible assessments that reduce barriers; emphasize authentic demonstrations of learning; and maintain rigorous academic expectations. In partnership with Justin Romack, Assistant Director at the Disability Resources Office, this workshop explores how assessment design influences student access and success. It examines common barriers students encounter in traditional assessments and discusses practical strategies for designing assessments that provide multiple pathways for students to demonstrate their learning. Participants will also discover how generative AI can support brainstorming alternative assessment formats, applying UDL principles to assessments, and simplifying assignment language. Learning Outcomes: Participants will be able to… 1) Identify common barriers in traditional assessment design that may limit student access and opportunities to demonstrate learning. 2) Apply Universal Design for Learning (UDL) principles to design or revise assessments. 3) Identify ways generative AI can assist with creating alternative assessment formats and redesigning assessments.

description: Our loyalties profoundly shape how we interpret events, information, and people, often in ways we don't recognize. title: ELP Special Topics in Grammar for Speech
description: Do you have questions about English grammar that haven't been covered in a workshop or need additional practice with a challenging grammar topic? Special Topics in Grammar for Speech is an interactive drop-in session where participants can ask questions about grammar for spoken communication and receive individualized guidance. Discussions may focus on topics such as verb tenses, modal verbs, question formation, articles, passive voice, or any other grammar questions participants bring. Practice activities will be tailored to attendees' needs, providing opportunities to apply new learning by practicing speaking using realistic scenarios. The goal is to enhance grammatical accuracy, spoken fluency, and confidence. Participants will be able to: 1. Identify situations in academic and instructional communication where accurate grammar is essential for conveying meaning clearly. 2. Produce appropriate grammatical structures in spoken English, applying individualized feedback to improve accuracy and comprehensibility. 3. Monitor and revise their own spoken grammar while communicating in academic and professional contexts.

title: American English Vowel System (Part 4 of 4)
description: The vowel sounds of American English are challenging to learners of English because there are so many, and because English spelling does not convey the pronunciation predictably. This four-session series of interactive workshops aims to increase attendees' phonological awareness, and as a result, their listening and intelligibility. Through a variety of activities and handouts, attendees will become familiar with each vowel and with resources to practice listening discrimination and pronunciation on their own. Each attendee has the opportunity to get personalized feedback on their own pronunciation. This event is restricted to those who attended Part 1 (register for that at https://ers.tamu.edu/event/10678).
classification_reasoning_summary: Event is academic, research, or career oriented.

title: Workshop: Leading with Integrity: Giving and Receiving Criticism
description: It’s hard to receive criticism without feeling defensive, ashamed, or angry, and it’s hard to give criticism without worrying about damaging your relationships. As a result, we don’t give criticism even when we know that we should, and we don’t learn from criticism that could have helped us grow. For groups, organizations, and leaders who value honesty and accountability, this is a serious problem, but there are steps that we can take to both give and receive criticism with greater ease and effectiveness.

title: Workshop: Leading with Integrity: Giving and Receiving Criticism
description: It’s hard to receive criticism without feeling defensive, ashamed, or angry, and it’s hard to give criticism without worrying about damaging your relationships. title: ELP Special Topics in Grammar for Speech
description: Do you have questions about English grammar that haven't been covered in a workshop or need additional practice with a challenging grammar topic? Special Topics in Grammar for Speech is an interactive drop-in session where participants can ask questions about grammar for spoken communication and receive individualized guidance. Discussions may focus on topics such as verb tenses, modal verbs, question formation, articles, passive voice, or any other grammar questions participants bring. Practice activities will be tailored to attendees' needs, providing opportunities to apply new learning by practicing speaking using realistic scenarios. title: American English Vowel System (Part 3 of 4)
description: The vowel sounds of American English are challenging to learners of English because there are so many, and because English spelling does not convey the pronunciation predictably. This four-session series of interactive workshops aims to increase attendees' phonological awareness, and as a result, their listening and intelligibility. Through a variety of activities and handouts, attendees will become familiar with each vowel and with resources to practice listening discrimination and pronunciation on their own. Each attendee has the opportunity to get personalized feedback on their own pronunciation. title: Workshop: Leading with Integrity: Giving and Receiving Criticism
description: It’s hard to receive criticism without feeling defensive, ashamed, or angry, and it’s hard to give criticism without worrying about damaging your relationships. As a result, we don’t give criticism even when we know that we should, and we don’t learn from criticism that could have helped us grow. For groups, organizations, and leaders who value honesty and accountability, this is a serious problem, but there are steps that we can take to both give and receive criticism with greater ease and effectiveness.

title: Workshop: When Loyalties Collide: What Does It Mean to Lead in an Era of Conflicting Loyalties?
description: Our loyalties profoundly shape how we interpret events, information, and people, often in ways we don't recognize. Studies consistently show that two people with different loyalties can witness the same situation and reach completely opposite conclusions. This makes it essential for leaders to critically examine their own loyalties: Why are we loyal to certain ideas, people, or groups? Are these loyalties justified? When should we reconsider or even abandon a loyalty? In this workshop we will explore various definitions and theories of loyalty, which will help you to develop practical frameworks for navigating conflicting loyalties and leading with moral clarity.

title: Workshop: When Loyalties Collide: What Does It Mean to Lead in an Era of Conflicting Loyalties?
description: Our loyalties profoundly shape how we interpret events, information, and people, often in ways we don't recognize. Studies consistently show that two people with different loyalties can witness the same situation and reach completely opposite conclusions. This makes it essential for leaders to critically examine their own loyalties: Why are we loyal to certain ideas, people, or groups? Are these loyalties justified? When should we reconsider or even abandon a loyalty? In this workshop we will explore various definitions and theories of loyalty, which will help you to develop practical frameworks for navigating conflicting loyalties and leading with moral clarity.

title: Workshop: When Loyalties Collide: What Does It Mean to Lead in an Era of Conflicting Loyalties?
description: Our loyalties profoundly shape how we interpret events, information, and people, often in ways we don't recognize. Studies consistently show that two people with different loyalties can witness the same situation and reach completely opposite conclusions. This makes it essential for leaders to critically examine their own loyalties: Why are we loyal to certain ideas, people, or groups? Are these loyalties justified? When should we reconsider or even abandon a loyalty? In this workshop we will explore various definitions and theories of loyalty, which will help you to develop practical frameworks for navigating conflicting loyalties and leading with moral clarity.

Participants improve spontaneous speaking, active listening, and conversational turn-taking. Through communication with speakers from a variety of backgrounds, they acclimate to different accents. The sessions promote social connections, intercultural dialogue, and a sense of belonging. The goal is to enhance English fluency, comprehension, and confidence. Learning Outcomes: Participants will be able to: 1. Employ effective spontaneous communication skills in social, academic and professional settings. 2. Elaborate on their viewpoints and opinions in group discussions. 3. Construct clear and well-structured responses during impromptu conversations. 4. Apply appropriate turn-taking and active listening techniques in casual group discussions and more formal academic discussions.
classification_reasoning_summary: Event is academic, research, or career oriented.

description: Fifth in a series of workshops for graduate students, post-docs, and visiting scholars whose primary language is not English. title: The Higher-Impact Classroom: Elevating Current Practices Without Increasing Workload
description: Facilitators: Nate Poling, Center for Teaching Excellence Description:Every instructor wants their students to deeply engage, retain knowledge, and succeed, yet the term "High-Impact Practices" can feel like an overwhelming mandate that requires a major remodeling of your course. This workshop strips away the administrative jargon to focus on a sustainable approach: making your existing courses higher-impact. By auditing the assignments and activities you already use, we will explore how small, intentional design tweaks can boost student engagement, success, and retention. Whether you teach a large lecture or a small seminar, this session offers a universal framework to elevate your teaching practices without inflating your grading workload. This foundational overview aligns with institutional goals while connecting you directly to customized CTE consultation support. Learning Outcomes: Participants will be able to… 1) Modify one existing course assignment to increase student engagement without increasing their grading workload.

title: ELP Special Topics in Grammar for Speech
description: Do you have questions about English grammar that haven't been covered in a workshop or need additional practice with a challenging grammar topic? Special Topics in Grammar for Speech is an interactive drop-in session where participants can ask questions about grammar for spoken communication and receive individualized guidance. Discussions may focus on topics such as verb tenses, modal verbs, question formation, articles, passive voice, or any other grammar questions participants bring. Practice activities will be tailored to attendees' needs, providing opportunities to apply new learning by practicing speaking using realistic scenarios. The goal is to enhance grammatical accuracy, spoken fluency, and confidence. Participants will be able to: 1. Identify situations in academic and instructional communication where accurate grammar is essential for conveying meaning clearly. 2. Produce appropriate grammatical structures in spoken English, applying individualized feedback to improve accuracy and comprehensibility. 3. Monitor and revise their own spoken grammar while communicating in academic and professional contexts.

Apply appropriate turn-taking and active listening techniques in casual group discussions and more formal academic discussions.
